headline: Council sent $3,502,413 in new growth to the new high school fund and approved a 6-5 residential tax rate of 12.87 per thousand.
summary: The commercial rate is 28.35 per thousand, and a rate on line 252 failed 5-6. Council also voted 11-0 to raise public speaking time for all speakers from 30 minutes to 60 minutes. The change of the council start time to 6:00 p.m. was held under privilege. Requests on body-worn camera footage, building permits on contaminated land, and sports field access went to the city manager.
decisions: Approved 10-1 sending the $3,502,413 in new growth above budget to the new high school fund.
Failed 5-6: the tax rate on line 252, 13.16 per thousand for residents and 27.29 for commercial property.
Approved 6-5 the tax rate on line 276, 12.87 per thousand for residents and 28.35 for commercial property.
Referred petition 9A to the planning board.
Referred to the city manager a request for a report on releasing body-worn camera footage, 911 calls and dispatch communications involving elected officials; the vote was unanimous.
Recommitted to the MLO Committee the chairman's order asking for a City Council budget priority process, 11-0.
Held under privilege, which puts off the proposal to start council meetings at 6:00 p.m. instead of 5:30 p.m.
Approved 11-0 changing public speaking time for all speakers from 30 minutes to 60 minutes.
Sent to the city manager a request for a City Solicitor report on whether the council can deny building permits for housing on contaminated land.
Sent to the city manager an order to discuss sports field availability with the School Department.
discussion: Tax rates: Members argued over whether to set the lowest residential rate or keep business rates lower to attract jobs. Some said homeowners cannot afford an increase. The council chose line 276 on a 6-5 vote.

Public meeting time and comment: Public speakers said a 5:30 start would keep working residents from attending. They also said limiting comment on held items would silence residents. Council members said the changes would make meetings more efficient.

Sports field access: Youth and families asked for free public hours at locked turf fields. The city said the locked fields are synthetic fields used by leagues, and the city manager has asked to meet with the group.
Body-worn camera footage: Speakers asked for one standard for releasing police video and 911 calls involving elected officials. They cited a September 2026 crash involving a councilor.

Contaminated land near homes: Speakers said an old dump near Suburban Road could pose health risks during construction. The city said state and local rules already require cleanup, and a third-party review of soil tests is being finished.
